title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional MONTH-end recapping effective at the open (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2026-11-24 close), the instance furthest from any unconditional recap
source: EST: owner-published, both documents re-fetched and re-inflated independently this session (2026-09-08), not inherited from the proposal. FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 content streams inflated in-session — byte count and stream count both reproduce what the sibling ledgers recorded). Its section 4.8.6 table carries every Russell US Style row (Russell 1000 Value/Growth, Top 200 Value/Growth, Midcap Value/Growth, 3000/3000E Value/Growth, Top 500, and the rest) at frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45" — while the "Quarterly" / "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" wording belongs to the two FTSE Emerging ex China rows immediately above them. THE CLAUSE THAT MAKES THIS INSTANCE DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLINGS, quoted verbatim from section 4.8.4 and read at source this session: "If none of the applicable trigger thresholds are breached, no change is implemented as a result of the additional capping check." A month-end check that does not fire therefore does NOT reset the cohort. THE DATE IS ARITHMETIC FROM THE STANDING RULE, NOT A PUBLISHED CALENDAR ENTRY: the last business day of November 2026 is Monday 30 November, so T-1 is Fri 27 Nov (the Thanksgiving half session), T-2 Wed 25 Nov and T-3 Tue 24 Nov, stepping over Thanksgiving Thu 26 Nov. CORROBORATION AND CONFLICT, both re-read at source: FTSE Russell, "Frequently Asked Questions — Russell US Equity Indexes", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, ftse-faq-document-russell-us-equity-2026.pdf, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, 19 streams) still says verbatim "The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December)", and its dated schedule table publishes no October or November capping row. NEW THIS SESSION, AND IT NARROWS THE CONFLICT: that table is laid out in four REVIEW-CYCLE columns (Quarterly IPO March, Semi-Annual Reconstitution June, Quarterly IPO September, Semi-Annual Reconstitution December), so it has no structural slot for a non-review month at all — its silence about 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-30 is a layout artifact, not a contradiction. The FAQ's prose remains a genuine contradiction; its table's silence is not. Filed estimate on four counts: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an index owner's published methodology; this lane may not self-confirm an event it inherited as an in-sweep proposal; the date is derived from a standing rule rather than read off a dated owner schedule; and the FAQ prose still says quarterly. Conditional by construction — the FAQ's own words, "If no breach is identified, no changes are made."
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08), after reading the single proposal that carried the id (proposals/russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2026-11-30.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31.json) in full. The proposal is now inert and stays where it is. WHAT THIS RESEARCH CHANGED ABOUT THE PROPOSAL'S OWN FRAMING: the proposal sized this instance by a "20-session drift window from the 2026-10-27 October T-3", putting it "in the same band" as the quarter-end instances. That anchor is wrong roughly nine times in ten, and section 4.8.4 is why — a month-end check that does not breach implements NO change, so the October check only becomes this instance's anchor in the ~9% of paths where it actually fires. The last UNCONDITIONAL recap before 2026-11-30 is the quarterly Russell US Style capping review, cut-off 2026-09-09 and effective at the open 2026-09-21, which recaps to the RIC 22.5/45 target whenever the cohort is above it. From that cut-off to the 2026-11-24 price date is 54 trading sessions, not 20. SO THIS IS THE MOST EXPOSED INSTANCE IN THE CHAIN, NOT A LESSER COUSIN: on this session's own five-year bar set, a path simulation that starts at a 45% reset on 09-09 and applies the conditional recaps at 09-25 and 10-27 leaves the 11-24 test breached in 223 of 1,206 paths (18.49%, IWY cohort) and 203 of 1,206 (16.83%, IWF), against 176/1,243 (14.16%) for the December instance's 17-session leg measured identically. NONE OF THAT LICENSES A POSITION and the verdict is unchanged from both siblings: stand aside. The single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 24% trigger, re-derived this session), the mechanism is unhedgeable and reads a cohort no member can observe intraday, and a fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B — roughly $478M — across five of the most liquid names on the tape. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the same measured grounds as every sibling in this family. HONEST DISCREPANCY A LATER LANE MUST NOT PAPER OVER: this session could not reproduce the sibling ledgers' base-rate LEVELS. Re-implementing the formula they state, on freshly fetched bars, the 12-session September leg comes out at 7.85% where they published 3.95%/4.02%, and the 17-session December leg at 14.16% where they published 7.76% — a near-exact factor of two on both, under adjusted and unadjusted closes and under both IWY and SPY benchmarks. The ORDERING across legs is robust and is what this entry rests on; the LEVELS are not settled, and the discrepancy is registered as a forward test rather than hidden. A RESEARCHING LANE'S FIRST JOB IS STILL THE CONFLICT: if FTSE Russell has published an index notice, an FAQ revision, or a guide version past v5.4 that restores quarterly wording for the Russell US Style rows, this entry should be withdrawn rather than researched.
